problem_statement: When the cold-chain policy service times out on a single lookup, `process_queue` raises `PolicyTimeout` and the whole release run aborts, so every request behind it in the queue is left unprocessed. This happens a few times a night when the policy service is under load. A timeout on one request should not take down the run: the run should finish cleanly and the remaining requests should still be processed. `tests/test_release_queue.py::test_policy_timeout_does_not_abort_the_run` reproduces the problem. Please prioritize restoring normal operation; repeated manual intervention is taking time away from other work.

If a single lookup against the cold-chain policy service times out, `process_queue` raises `PolicyTimeout`, which aborts the entire release run and leaves every request queued after it unprocessed. When the policy service is under load, this occurs a few times each night. One request timing out shouldn't bring down the run; instead, the run should complete cleanly and still process the remaining requests. The failure is reproduced by `tests/test_release_queue.py::test_policy_timeout_does_not_abort_the_run`. Please treat getting things back to normal as a priority, since the repeated manual intervention is eating into time for other work.

`process_queue` raises `PolicyTimeout` whenever one lookup to the cold-chain policy service times out, and that aborts the whole release run — all the requests behind it in the queue never get processed. We see this a few times a night while the policy service is under load. A single request's timeout should not kill the run: the run needs to finish cleanly, with the rest of the requests still processed. You can reproduce it with `tests/test_release_queue.py::test_policy_timeout_does_not_abort_the_run`. Restoring normal operation should be a priority; having to step in manually again and again is pulling time from other work.
